neighbours.label: A one-letter variable standing for data or model quantities in statistics or machine learning, in code or prose: the target y, the data matrix X, weights w or W, the bias b. Quiet for the same letters with other meanings (a grade, a name like Malcolm X, the letter itself, Spanish 'y'), for spelled-out names (labels, target, bias, outcome), and weak for plain algebra or physics letters, for mu, and for a letter that is the very first token of the text.
fire: We fit the regression by predicting y from the feature matrix X using ordinary least squares.
In the training loop, the gradient of the loss with respect to w is computed and the weights are updated.
The model learns a bias b so that the decision boundary does not have to pass through the origin.
After standardizing the columns of X, the ridge solution for w becomes much more stable.
Each row of X is one patient, and y records whether that patient was readmitted.
The weight matrix W in the first layer maps 784 pixel inputs to 128 hidden units.
quiet: We fit the regression by predicting the outcome from the feature matrix using ordinary least squares.
In the training loop, the gradient of the loss with respect to the weights is computed and they are updated.
The model learns a bias term so that the decision boundary does not have to pass through the origin.
She got a B on her statistics exam after studying the ridge regression chapter all week.
Malcolm X gave a famous speech that students still analyze in history class.
Each row of the table is one patient, and the target column records whether they were readmitted.
The word 'yacht' is one of the few English words where the letter y follows a silent pattern.
